Chapter Two: Identifying and Challenging Internal Barriers
Now that we've started building a more open and accepting view of creativity, let’s talk about something that often stands in our way—those internal obstacles that quietly block our creative flow. Funny enough, these barriers aren’t usually out there in the world. Most of the time, they’re tucked inside us, shaped by old beliefs, fears, or habits we’ve carried for years without even noticing.
One of the biggest hurdles is something I like to call the “Censor.” You know that critical inner voice? The one that pipes up with doubts, second-guessing, and quick judgments whenever you try something new or creative? Sometimes, it sounds suspiciously like a teacher, a parent, or just society whispering that creative work isn’t practical or worthwhile. The Censor tells us our ideas are silly, that we’ll never measure up, or that it’s not even worth trying. And wow, does it love perfectionism and comparison—two things that can really drain the fun right out of creativity.
The trick is to recognize the Censor for what it is—a protective mechanism that, while trying to keep us safe, actually ends up holding us back. Once you spot that voice and name it, you can start to separate your real creative spark from all that noisy self-criticism.
So, how do you quiet the Censor? There are a few strategies that really help:
First, try using affirmations. This is about swapping out those harsh, negative thoughts for something kinder and more encouraging. Instead of telling yourself, “I’m not talented enough,” what if you said, “I’m willing to learn and grow creatively”? It’s not about pretending everything’s perfect—it’s about giving yourself a more supportive inner environment to work in.
Another approach is to take on simple creative recovery tasks. Think of these as small, low-pressure creative acts—like doodling in the margins of your notebook, writing a short poem, or even experimenting with a new recipe. The idea is just to experience the satisfaction of making something, no matter how modest. Every little success proves to yourself that you really are creative.
Also, it’s worth spending a little time examining your limiting beliefs. Where did that feeling of “I’m not creative” actually come from? Whose voice are you really hearing? When you start to shine a light on these old stories, they lose a lot of their power.
And then there’s another big barrier: the fear of looking foolish or making mistakes. How many times have we hesitated to try something new, just because we’re worried about being judged? But here’s the thing—creativity thrives on experimentation and risk. Mistakes aren’t signs of failure; they’re proof that you’re exploring and growing.
To build up your resilience, it helps to adopt a mindset of curiosity and self-compassion. Instead of aiming for flawless results, focus on the process of learning and discovery. Each creative step, no matter how small, is a chance to practice courage—and to be a bit kinder to yourself along the way.
Over time, these simple practices loosen the grip of the Censor and other internal barriers. The creative part of you—that voice that might’ve been quiet for a while—starts to speak up again. Sure, there will still be setbacks and moments of doubt. That’s totally normal. But with patience and persistence, you’ll find it’s possible to move through resistance and rediscover just how joyful it can be to make something new.
